status: FROZEN before running (user-approved plan of 2026-10-23); extension analysis: the week-2 and confirmation labels were already viewed for earlier models
question: given the same random-exposure labels, how much does adapting the collaborative representation gain over the tuned iALS, and how much do personalized attribute features add on top?

forms.C1_cf_interactions: 32 element-wise products u_k * v_k of the frozen tuned iALS factors (seed 0) plus the has-factors flag; ridge logistic regression; lambda in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}
forms.C2_L2_plus_cf: LR-L2 standardized columns (dev-6M statistics) plus the same 33 CF inputs; lambda in {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1}

inputs: interaction columns standardized with mean/sd fitted on the tune-group week-1 training rows only (fixed thereafter); rows without valid factors get zero interactions and flag 0
training_and_selection: identical to protocol_adaptation.json: fit on tune-group week-1 main-population scope-A rows, select lambda per form on report-group week-1 per-user AUC (ties within 0.0005 -> larger lambda), refit the selected lambda on all development week-1 rows
test: development users week 2 (04-29..05-08), scope A, main population; per-user AUC; paired user bootstrap 2000 seed 2026; iALS inputs seed 0 only (interaction weights are tied to one factor basis, so no seed averaging)
contrasts: C1 - iALS_tuned (gain from adapting the CF representation)
C2 - C1 (what attribute features add on top)
C2 - M3 (33 CF inputs vs the single iALS score)
decision_rule: +0.01 per-user AUC and 95% interval excluding 0, as before
evidence_level: extension analysis; original confirmation results and artifacts unchanged
